summary: The readiness wait is implemented, gated and committed on phase/019-P4 (2a15ede): control-plane nodes wait for /readyz; workers wait for their own Node to report Ready=True with a heartbeat later than the restart, read with the kubelet's credential through the local apiserver-proxy. It passed a stub harness (8 scenarios), and read-only probes on srvk8s1 and srvk8s4 matched. But the plan's premise that a failing handler 'stops the roll' is false for the un-serialised renew-internal-tls.yml (the Friday certs build): scratch runs on ansible-core 2.20.5 show that under throttle: 1, once one host fails the handler, the remaining hosts still run it, whether any_errors_fatal is unset, task-level or play-level. site-k8s.yml's serial: 1 apply does stop. Operator to decide how V12's 'stops the roll, a Friday certs build included' is met: (a) a peer precheck, where a control-plane node refuses to restart kubelite unless every other control-plane member of its k8s_<env> group answers /readyz; this also refuses every kubelite restart (converge or certs) while any peer is down for any reason, leaving that arg change or renewed leaf unloaded, with nothing re-notifying it on the next run; or (b) amend V12 so that in un-serialised plays a not-ready node only turns the run red, while the remaining nodes still restart one at a time.
